_readme: Elton draft. [[c:...]] is cyan = not confirmed. History from the Elton Parish Council short history unless noted.
name: The Black Horse

layers.essential_history: [[c:In the 1700s the Black Horse was the village post house, where travellers could change horses and post was collected.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:Overend, the road outside, is the old way south out of the village towards Elton Hall.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:A rider from the procession left a letter here to go by post. The post bag was torn in the night and half the letter is smudged.]]

sources.title: Elton Parish Council: A short history of Elton

directions_to_next: [[c:Head south, about 160 metres as the crow flies, to Overend. Carry on south along Overend. Keep to the pavements and paths.]]
support: [[c:Support the village: the Black Horse is still a working pub.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The torn letter]]
material: [[c:"...to Master Goldsmith of Cheapside, London. I have j_w_ls fit for a queen to sell. I will bring them within the week. R. H."]]
puzzle.question: [[c:What did R. H. plan to sell? (one word)]]
hints: [[c:The missing letters are E and E.]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:JEWELS. R. H. is Richard Hale. He planned to sell the Queen's jewels from the casket to a London goldsmith.]]

evidence: [[c:Richard Hale wrote to a London goldsmith offering to sell jewels.]]
